title: McDonald's Earnings Beat Estimates Despite Revenue Miss
excerpt: Adjusted EPS rose 11% to $3.57 as franchised margins grew, but revenue of $7.16 billion missed estimates and U.S. comparable sales slipped 0.2%; the dividend rises 4% to $1.93.
body:
• McDonald's third-quarter adjusted earnings rose 11% to $3.57 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.36, while revenue increased 1% to $7.16 billion and missed the $7.28 billion estimate.
  • Global comparable sales grew 1.5%: international markets offset a 0.2% decline in the U.S., where fewer guest visits were largely offset by higher average checks.
  • The franchise model carried the quarter — franchised revenues rose 3% to $4.49 billion and franchised restaurant margins grew 3% to $3.8 billion, about 90% of total restaurant margins.
  • Shareholders get a raise: McDonald's declared a 4% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.93 per share, and still plans about $3.7 billion of capital spending and roughly 2,500 restaurant openings in 2026.

McDonald's beat profit expectations in the third quarter of 2026 on the strength of its franchised business, even as revenue came in light and U.S. sales slipped. The Chicago-based burger chain reported on November 4 that adjusted earnings rose 11% to $3.57 per share, ahead of the $3.36 Zacks Consensus Estimate, while revenues increased 1% to $7.16 billion, missing the $7.28 billion consensus. GAAP earnings were $3.51 per share, up 10%, and net income rose 9% to $2.49 billion. The adjusted figure excludes $56 million of pre-tax restructuring charges, or $0.06 per share, tied to the company's Accelerating the Organization program.

"In the U.S., we're encouraged by improvement as the quarter progressed following our intervention on value."

— Chris Kempczinski, McDonald's Chairman and CEO

International sales carried global growth

Global comparable sales increased 1.5%, down from 3.6% growth in the year-ago quarter. U.S. comparable sales decreased 0.2% as negative guest counts were largely offset by positive check growth. International Operated Markets rose 1.4%, led by Germany and Australia and partly offset by France, while International Developmental Licensed Markets increased 4.2%, led by Japan and partly offset by negative comparable sales in China, the company said.

Systemwide sales — sales across all restaurants, franchised and company-owned — increased 4% to more than $38 billion. Loyalty programs remained a large part of that base: systemwide sales to loyalty members exceeded $11 billion in the quarter and reached $41 billion over the trailing twelve months across 70 markets. McDonald's ended September with 46,554 restaurants worldwide, according to Zacks.

Franchise margins did the heavy lifting

Franchised restaurant revenues increased 3% to $4.49 billion, while sales at company-owned and operated restaurants declined 3% to $2.48 billion and other revenues rose 26% to $189 million. Franchised restaurant margins increased 3% to $3.8 billion and represented about 90% of total restaurant margin dollars; company-owned restaurant margins were roughly flat at $392 million, with U.S. margins down 16% on inflationary cost pressures, Zacks reported.

Consolidated operating income rose 7% to $3.60 billion, and 8% excluding the restructuring charges, helped by higher other operating income and the franchised margin growth. Selling, general and administrative expenses declined 3%.

Expansion plans stay on track

Management kept its 2026 outlook in place. McDonald's still expects about $3.7 billion in capital expenditures, roughly 2,500 restaurant openings and about 2,100 net additions this year, an operating margin in the mid-to-high 40% range and an effective tax rate of 21% to 23%, according to Zacks' summary of the outlook. The declared dividend increase to $1.93 per share continues the company's long record of annual raises. What investors will watch next is the U.S. business: whether the late-quarter improvement Kempczinski cited turns into positive comparable sales in the fourth quarter after a quarter in which guest counts fell.
